When you call someone straitlaced, you mean they are extremely strict about morals, proper behavior, and social rules — and often uncomfortably so. A straitlaced person has a very rigid, conservative idea of what is right and wrong, and they hold themselves and others to those standards very tightly. They disapprove of anything that seems too loose, improper, rebellious, or morally "off."

Think of it as someone who has the dial of propriety turned all the way up, and the dial of flexibility turned all the way down.
The feel of the word — its connotation

This is important: straitlaced is almost always used critically or with a hint of disapproval. When you describe someone as straitlaced, you are implying that their strictness goes too far — that it makes them uptight, judgmental, or no fun to be around. It's rarely a compliment.

It's not the same as calling someone principled or disciplined, which sound respectful. Straitlaced has a slightly negative edge. It suggests the person is rigid in a way that limits them and others around them.
What a straitlaced person actually looks like in real life

To make this concrete, here's what straitlaced behavior and attitudes look like:

  • They are deeply uncomfortable with — or openly disapproving of — things like crude jokes, swearing, revealing clothing, casual relationships, or anything they see as "indecent."
  • They tend to follow social and moral rules very strictly, and they expect others to do the same.
  • They may refuse to participate in activities others consider perfectly normal fun, like certain parties, movies, or casual conversations.
  • They often come across as prim, uptight, humorless, or judgmental — even if they don't mean to be.
  • They may be shocked or offended by things most people consider minor or harmless.

• It does not mean someone is dishonest or hypocritical (though a straitlaced person could be).
  • It does not mean someone is boring in general — it specifically refers to strictness about morals and propriety.
  • It does not mean someone is unintelligent or uneducated. Straitlaced refers only to their social and moral rigidity.

While it most commonly describes people, straitlaced can also describe:

  • Attitudes or values: "Her straitlaced values made her uncomfortable around her college classmates."
  • Environments or communities: "He grew up in a straitlaced small town where everything was controlled."
  • Upbringings: "Her straitlaced upbringing meant she had never seen an R-rated movie."

• "He was so straitlaced that he refused to watch the film because it had a few bad words in it."
  • "The new manager's straitlaced attitude made the office feel tense and overly formal."
  • "Growing up in a straitlaced household, she wasn't allowed to listen to rock music."
  • "For someone so straitlaced, he was surprisingly kind and open to listening."

These words share the same general territory as straitlaced, each with a slightly different shade:

  • Prudish — overly shocked by anything related to sex or the body
  • Puritanical — extremely strict about moral and religious rules (references the Puritan religious tradition)
  • Prim — excessively proper and easily shocked; overly neat and correct in manner
  • Priggish — self-righteously moral, and smug about it
  • Uptight — tense and uncomfortable with anything informal or improper (more informal/casual word)
  • Rigid — unwilling to change or bend rules (broader word, not only about morals)

• Permissive — allowing a lot of freedom; not strict
  • Open-minded — willing to consider different ways of living and thinking
  • Broad-minded — tolerant of other people's choices and behaviors
  • Easygoing — relaxed and not easily bothered
  • Liberal — in the social sense, tolerant of a wide range of behaviors and lifestyles
One final way to remember it

Imagine someone who has laced their corset so tightly that they can barely breathe or move — they're stiff, uncomfortable, and unable to relax. That image captures straitlaced perfectly: morally and socially so tight and rigid that there's no room to bend, breathe, or enjoy life freely.
